Recorded as indirect with unknown intermediates because the two datasets disagree. In the pooled systematic review hematocrit was independently associated with venous thrombosis, but not with thrombosis overall, where age dominated; the 41-patient single-centre series found no association at all. Whatever connects a raised hematocrit to a thrombotic event in this disease is therefore not established, and it is at most a partial contribution alongside conventional risk factors.

Smoking was independently associated with arterial thrombotic events on multivariable analysis of the pooled literature. Recorded as predisposing rather than triggering, and with unknown intermediates, because nothing in the cited work measures a step between the exposure and the event in these patients.

Smokers were over-represented among the patients reporting hyperviscosity symptoms. Whether that is a viscosity effect, a carbon monoxide effect on oxygen unloading, or confounding by cardiovascular risk is not resolved by the cited analysis, which is why the intermediates are left unknown.

nodes.description: A heterozygous germline HBB missense variant substitutes a residue of the beta-globin chain that, for the alleles modelled here, participates in the allosteric transition of the hemoglobin tetramer rather than in heme coordination: a contact at the alpha1-beta2 sliding interface, a C-terminal residue holding a deoxy-state salt bridge, or a residue of the central-cavity 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate pocket. A further reported route, not branched here, alters the environment of the heme and the oxygen binding site itself. The activity the variant protein loses is the carrier activity rather than the binding activity: GO defines oxygen carrier activity as binding oxygen and delivering it to an acceptor, and these variants keep - indeed strengthen - the binding half while impairing the delivery half, which is why the modifier here is ABNORMAL rather than DECREASED. The mutant chain assembles into hemoglobin normally; what changes is the energy balance between the two quaternary states.

nodes.description: The peritubular interstitial fibroblasts of the renal cortex are the oxygen sensors that set erythropoietin output. Falling interstitial oxygen tension is transduced through the prolyl hydroxylase-HIF axis in these cells, the same axis whose germline lesions cause the oxygen-sensing erythrocytoses (VHL, EGLN1, EPAS1). Here the sensor and its transducers are intact and are responding correctly to a genuinely hypoxic signal, which is the crucial difference from those diseases: the drive is appropriate to the tissue oxygen tension and inappropriate only to the red cell mass.

nodes.description: 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate binds in the central cavity of deoxyhemoglobin and protons act at the Bohr sites; both are heterotropic effectors that hold the tetramer in the low-affinity state and couple oxygen release to local metabolic conditions. Substitutions at those binding sites leave the effectors present but unable to act, so the dissociation curve no longer responds normally to them. This is the mirror image of bisphosphoglycerate mutase deficiency, where the hemoglobin is normal and the effector is missing - a separate disease that reaches the same left-shifted curve.

The case against routine phlebotomy is specific to this disease: the red cell mass is the compensation for a left-shifted dissociation curve, so removing it removes oxygen-carrying capacity the patient is relying on, and the single-centre series found no correlation between hematocrit or phlebotomy and symptoms and concluded that the therapeutic value of phlebotomy is limited.

nodes.description: Smoking is not a cause of this disease, but it acts on it twice over. It adds a carbon monoxide load, and carboxyhemoglobin shifts the oxygen dissociation curve further to the left on top of the variant, so the same genotype should unload less oxygen in a smoker; and in the pooled cohorts smoking is associated with the two things carriers are actually at risk of - hyperviscosity symptoms and arterial thrombosis. That is why smoking cessation, rather than phlebotomy, is the first management measure in the review literature.
